title: Spotting thinking traps
content: Identify the cognitive distortion behind a distressing thought (all-or-nothing thinking, catastrophizing, mind-reading, over-generalizing, discounting the positive), then examine the evidence and reframe it more flexibly.
source: Cognitive behavioral therapy — cognitive distortions (standard clinical exercise)

title: Behavioral experiment planner
content: Write down an anxious prediction and how strongly you believe it, design a small real-world test, then record what actually happened versus what you feared.

metadata.prompt: What are you afraid will happen? How strongly do you believe it (0-100%)? What small experiment could test it, and what will you watch for?

title: Activity schedule
content: Plan small pleasant or meaningful activities across the day and rate your mood before and after, rebuilding momentum through action rather than waiting for motivation.

metadata.prompt: List two or three small activities you could do today — one pleasant, one meaningful. When will you do each, and how do you predict you'll feel afterward?

title: Pros and cons
content: Weigh a decision or urge by listing the benefits and costs of acting versus not acting, making the trade-offs visible instead of tangled.
source: Dialectical behavior therapy — pros and cons (standard clinical exercise)

metadata.prompt: For the choice on your mind: what are the pros and cons of doing it, and the pros and cons of not doing it?

title: Self-compassion letter
content: Write to yourself about a struggle from the perspective of a warm, understanding friend who knows your history and wants the best for you.

metadata.prompt: Write a short letter to yourself about what you're going through, in the voice of a kind friend who fully understands and accepts you.

title: Three good things
content: Recall three things that went well recently and reflect on why each happened, gently retraining attention toward the positive.
source: Positive psychology — three good things (standard clinical exercise)

metadata.prompt: What are three things — big or small — that went well recently? For each, why do you think it happened?

title: Fear ladder (exposure hierarchy)
content: List situations you avoid because of fear and rank them from least to most anxiety-provoking, creating a step-by-step ladder to face gradually.
source: Cognitive behavioral therapy — exposure hierarchy (standard clinical exercise)

metadata.prompt: List a few situations you avoid because they make you anxious, then rank them from easiest to hardest. Which one feels like a doable first step?

title: Worry decision tree
content: Sort a worry: is it about something you can act on now? If yes, plan one step; if no, practice letting it go or scheduling it for later.
source: Cognitive behavioral therapy — worry management (standard clinical exercise)

metadata.prompt: Write the worry on your mind. Is it something you can do something about right now? If yes, what's one step? If no, what would help you set it down?

title: Coping card
content: Create a short, personal reminder of what helps — coping steps, supportive people, and reasons to keep going — to reach for in a hard moment.

metadata.prompt: What helps you get through a hard moment? List a few coping steps, one or two people you could reach out to, and one reason worth holding onto.

title: Sleep diary
content: Track bedtime, wake time, and how rested you feel, along with caffeine, screens, and stress, to spot patterns affecting your sleep.

metadata.prompt: For last night: when did you go to bed and wake up, how rested do you feel (0-10), and what might have helped or hurt your sleep (caffeine, screens, stress)?

title: Letter to your future self
content: Write to yourself a few months or a year from now — what you hope for, what you're working through, and what you want to remember.

metadata.prompt: Write a short letter to yourself six months from now. What are you going through, what do you hope for, and what do you want future-you to remember about this time?
